title: systemd socket activation is declared but unimplemented; personad deletes systemd's socket
description:
systemd/personad.socket declares 'ListenStream=%t/persona/workload.sock' + RuntimeDirectory=persona, i.e. socket activation. Nothing implements it:

- grep for LISTEN_FDS / sd_listen_fds across the tree returns zero hits. personad never inherits a listener.
- personad/src/main.rs:52-54 builds its own PathBuf('/run/user/{uid}/persona/workload.sock') and passes it to server::serve.
- persona-grpc/src/server.rs:19-22 unconditionally does remove_file() on any existing socket, then binds its own at line 28.

So when the socket unit is enabled, systemd binds and listens; the first client connection name-activates personad.service; personad then DELETES systemd's listening socket and binds a fresh one. The connection that triggered activation is dropped, and systemd still holds an orphaned listener on an unlinked inode. Every socket-activated client fails.

Additional unit defects on the same root cause:
- systemd/personad.service has no Requires=personad.socket, no After=personad.socket, and no '[Install] Also=personad.socket'. Enabling the service does not enable the socket and vice versa.
- Type=simple, so systemd has no readiness signal; Type=notify would be required for correct activation ordering.
- RuntimeDirectory=persona/RuntimeDirectoryMode=0700 exists only on the .socket unit. Started standalone via personad.service, the directory is instead created by server.rs:24-26 create_dir_all() under the process umask (typically 0755), not 0700. The parent directory permissions differ depending on how the daemon was started.

Fix is a fork: either implement LISTEN_FDS inheritance in personad and stop binding a path, or drop personad.socket entirely and keep the self-bind path. Shipping both as-is means the unit files are broken.
close_reason: STALE -- no defect remains. systemd/personad.socket was deleted in 930072e ('fix: name the systemd unit consistently, drop the socket unit'), which resolved the fork the bead names in favour of keeping the self-bind path. Verified 2026-09-14: ls systemd/ shows only personad.service; grep for LISTEN_FDS/sd_listen_fds across the tree returns zero hits (as it should, since nothing declares socket activation any more); no file in the repo references personad.socket. The bead's secondary defects are moot with it: Requires=/After=/Also= would point at a unit that does not exist, and Type=notify was only needed for activation ordering. The RuntimeDirectoryMode=0700 concern is separately handled in code -- server.rs prepare_socket_dir creates the socket directory 0700 regardless of how the daemon was started, so the permissions no longer differ by launch method.
